tagline: Leading water and wastewater services provider delivering clean water and essential services to over 4.3 million households and businesses across the UK Midlands and mid-Wales
hero_kpi_rationale: Regulated revenue represents over 83% of total turnover and constitutes the structural pillar of the business model, with high visibility due to Ofwat regulation.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total value of sales generated by the company during the year.
kpis.description: Total revenue reached £1,856.7 million in 2014, up 1.4% compared to £1,831.6 million in 2013.
kpis.signal: Moderate growth driven by the regulated segment and non-regulated services.

kpis.name: Profit Before Tax
kpis.explanation: Profit generated before taxation, measuring operational profitability.
kpis.description: Profit before tax surged to £282.7 million in 2014, up 41.2% from £200.2 million in 2013, driven by growth in regulated PBIT and accounting adjustments.
kpis.signal: Significant jump due to stronger regulated performance and a low prior-year base.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditure (Capex)
kpis.explanation: Amount invested in physical assets to improve water and wastewater services.
kpis.description: Capex reached £602 million in 2014, an 8% increase, to strengthen water and wastewater infrastructure across the Midlands and mid-Wales region.
kpis.signal: Marked capex increase, aligned with regulatory commitments and infrastructure improvements.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount distributed to shareholders per share held.
kpis.description: Dividend per share increased to 80.4 pence in 2014, up 6.0% from 75.85 pence in 2013, reflecting the strength of regulated cash flow.
kpis.signal: Steady dividend growth, consistent with distribution policy and reflecting robust regulated cash flow.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: The group employed 8,289 people as of March 31, 2014 (5,902 at Severn Trent Water and 2,387 at Severn Trent Services), stable compared to the previous year.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount despite revenue growth, indicating operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Regulatory Capital Value
kpis.explanation: Regulatory value of regulated assets, the basis for calculating permitted revenues set by Ofwat.
kpis.description: RCV increased to £7,618 million as of March 31, 2014, up 3.4% from £7,364 million in 2013, supported by investments and Ofwat regulation.
kpis.signal: RCV growth reflecting significant investments and an expanding base of regulated assets.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €15.91 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €9.7 Bn in the latest year

risks.title: Tariff regulation and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned at the beginning of the document, with strong language ("below inflation", "lowest bills"). It is central in every annual communication, reflecting ongoing and increasing regulatory pressure. The Regulation category dominates the sector.

risks.title: Increased competition due to market reform
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the Water Act 2014 and the company's intention to "exploit the changes" related to competition. The language is proactive but acknowledges a structural shift. This risk has been evolving for several years.

risks.title: Insufficient asset quality performance
risks.score_rationale: The Chief Executive acknowledges that 3 out of 20 indicators are below standard, with serviceability areas deemed "marginal". The tone is concerned and corrective actions are announced. This risk is recurring.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of critical infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly mentioned in the excerpt, UK water companies are classified as critical infrastructure. The risk is implicit but high in intensity and potential impact, consistent with recent sector standards.

risks.title: Dependence on Ofwat decisions
risks.score_rationale: The document refers to Ofwat and the Price Review process multiple times. The tone is cooperative but reflects total dependence. This structural risk is central and repeated annually.

risks.title: Reduction of pollution incidents
risks.score_rationale: The report mentions a reduction of over one-third in pollution incidents, but acknowledges ongoing efforts. The language shows improvement, but a high residual risk remains in case of recurrence.

risks.title: Poor performance in the non-regulated segment
risks.score_rationale: The document reports a loss in the Products division and disappointing performance, despite gains in Operating Services. The tone is mixed, with turnaround plans announced.

risks.title: Operational safety and industrial risks
risks.score_rationale: The document highlights safety as a priority, with accident rates among the lowest in the sector. However, the risk is inherent to industrial operations and remains high on the agenda.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the 2014 annual report. The strategy focuses on regulated water services, operational efficiency, and renewable energy.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation.
Absence of digital projects or data-driven technological innovation.
Focus on physical infrastructure, Ofwat regulation, and customer service improvement.
